To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ITIPs are usually overvalued by financial option pricing models and that this overvaluation can be explained by the fact that the models do not consider idiosyncratically distributed cashflows, an incomplete market and a risk-averse decision maker.
ITIP decision making should take into account that the discounted cashflows as well as the runtime of ITIPs are uncertain and the market is incomplete.
the consideration of the runtime to be unknown, the market to be in- complete, and the cashflow to be uncertain, usually lead to a lower risk-adjusted value of an ITIP’s option to expand.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the valuation of ITIPs can be improved by means of more appropriate assumptions in the underlying real option analysis approach.
the question of how to value ITIPs in an exante decision making process.
the development and evaluation of a simulation model that is able to value ITIPs in a way that better reflects their specific characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ITIP valuation by means of the presented model leads to lower riskadjusted option values than ITIP valuation by the Black–Sloles model.
the use of standard option pricing models for the valuation of ITIPs should be restricted to the case of risk-neutral investors.
the valuation of ITIPs is more complex than it is usually assumed in the IS literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the valuation of real option in ITIPs is a very complex task and that it requires a more comprehensive model than the Black–Scheoles model.
the Black–Sloles model, as frequently used in IS literature for the valuation of managerial flexibilities, is not suitable for ITIPs and should be replaced by a more appropriate model.
the valuation of real option in ITIPs is not a straightforward task, and that the Black–Scheoles model is not the right model to use in this context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ITIP valuation models need to be adapted to reflect the characteristics of IT projects.
the consideration of idio-syncratic risk in the valuation of ITIPs is crucial for the decision-making of risk averse managers.
the use of the standard Black–Schoels model in ITIP decision-making is not recommended.
